clue.text: Where can you finds items in store so disorganised?

definitions.text: Where can you finds items in store

blocks.clueFragment: Where can you finds items in store
blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: everywhere throughout a shop
second meaning: a British idiom for chaotic and scattered

explanation.surface: A frustrated shopper can't find anything because the store's stock is in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer works literally (items are found everywhere in the store) and as the British idiom ALL OVER THE SHOP, meaning in a total mess.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something chaotic, scattered or confused, exactly what a badly organised store is.

clue.text: Complete dietary description appreciated by gluttons

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: a diet consisting of everything one is able to consume
second meaning: the restaurant offer of unlimited food for one price, loved by big eaters

explanation.surface: A nutritionist's thorough write-up of a diet finds favour among big eaters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complete' suggests thoroughness, but it means unlimited: the description is a buffet offer with no cap on helpings.
explanation.definitionFit: Restaurants advertise unlimited buffets with this phrase, which naturally attracts greedy diners wanting endless plates.

clue.text: Tied up leaders in long and complicated European debates

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so only the opening letter of each following word counts

blocks.note: the initials of these five words

explanation.surface: Drawn-out, convoluted debates in Europe have bogged things down.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoes are laced when their laces are tied, so laced means fastened or tied up with cord.

clue.text: Chance of success when Vatican replaces Head of Debt

indicators.note: one thing takes the place of the first letter of the word that follows, swapping out its opening

blocks.note: V is the international vehicle code for Vatican City
a debt is a financial liability

explanation.surface: A financial story: the Holy See takes over a loan, which improves its prospects.
explanation.walkthrough: The L at the head of LIABILITY is swapped for V, giving VIABILITY.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan's viability is its capacity to work in practice, its likelihood of succeeding.

clue.text: Frequent customer having predictable movements

blocks.note: first meaning: a patron who keeps coming back to a pub or shop
second meaning: an adjective for someone whose bowels work on schedule

explanation.walkthrough: 'Movements' looks like comings and goings of the customer, but the second sense is bowel movements.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub's regulars are its habitual patrons; a regular person, in the medical sense, has dependable bowel habits.

clue.text: Dangerous location from which to get stolen jumpers returned

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word for jumpers is read from its end

blocks.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
jumpers are tops; a jumper is the British word for a sweater

explanation.surface: A shady place where you could pick up pilfered sweaters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotspot is a place of danger or conflict, such as a military trouble zone.

clue.text: Reflect back some natural oscillations from the sun

indicators.note: some means only part of the next words is needed, a run of letters sitting inside them
a reflection shows things the other way round, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: letters running across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A physics note about natural vibrations whose energy bounces back from the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: The run RALOS sits across natuRAL OScillations; read backwards it gives SOLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Solar is the adjective for anything coming from or relating to the sun, like solar energy.

clue.text: Propose restricting route for this type of vehicle

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so one word closes around the other

blocks.note: to propose is to offer
a road is a route

explanation.surface: Someone suggests limiting which roads this kind of vehicle may use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Propose' is a verb in the surface, but it supplies a word that wraps around the route; 'this type of vehicle' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An off-roader is a rugged vehicle built for driving over rough ground away from paved roads.

clue.text: Lightly cover edges with a versatile material

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its two ends, so only its first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: first and last letters
first and last letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sewing advice: trim a garment's edges lightly with an adaptable fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is a stretchy synthetic fibre used in sportswear, swimwear and many other garments.

clue.text: Biographical advice for the dead boring

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: an instruction to obtain a written life story
second meaning: a curt retort to someone tediously dull, telling them to find some excitement

explanation.walkthrough: A life is a biography, so the brush-off can be read as advice to acquire one; 'dead' also hints that the deceased have no life.
explanation.definitionFit: The rude retort tells a tedious person to stop being dull and find more interesting things to do.

clue.text: Gather in support for impressive parade leader

blocks.note: grand means impressive
to marshal support is to gather it

explanation.surface: Rallying backing for someone who will lead a spectacular procession.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse clue order: the word from 'impressive' goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand marshal heads a parade, especially in American processions, as its honoured leading figure.

clue.text: Vintage poster depicting Boys in Blue

blocks.note: vintage means old
a bill is a printed poster

explanation.surface: An antique poster showing police officers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Bill is British slang for the police, who are also called the boys in blue from their uniforms.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British names for police officers, the second alluding to their dark blue uniforms.

clue.text: Rural post office converted into salon

indicators.note: a converted building has been remodelled, so these letters are rebuilt into another form

blocks.note: taken as written
PO is the standard abbreviation for post office

explanation.surface: A village post office has been turned into a hair or beauty salon.
explanation.definitionFit: A parlour is a shop offering a particular service, as in a beauty parlour, much like a salon.

clue.text: Island displays measure of interest in racing centre

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the letters at its heart are used
one item placed in another sits inside it, surrounded by the outer letters

blocks.note: the middle two of six letters
APR, annual percentage rate, measures the interest on a loan

explanation.surface: A racetrack shows how keen people are on a particular island.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an Italian island in the Bay of Naples, famous as a glamorous resort.

clue.text: Re-approve complicated approach to handling unwelcome cracks

definitions.note: a noun phrase for what the verb phrase does; the answer is a verb

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled, so the preceding letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: Bureaucratic sign-off as a messy way of glossing over a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: To paper over the cracks is to hide problems rather than fix them, as wallpaper hides cracked plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Papering over disguises flaws superficially, the idiom being specifically about concealing cracks instead of repairing them.

clue.text: Upset academic spoke at length

blocks.note: to rattle someone is to upset or unnerve them
a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A disgruntled lecturer droned on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like an adjective describing the academic, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle on is to chatter for a long time, talking rapidly and tediously.

clue.text: Old carrier with defect, one that damages the environment

blocks.note: a litter was a couch carried on poles, an old form of transport
a bug is a fault, as in software

explanation.surface: A faulty antique vehicle is polluting the surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: A litterbug carelessly drops rubbish in public places, spoiling the surroundings.

clue.text: Spotted outbreak contracted from child's waste container

definitions.text: Spotted outbreak contracted from child's waste container

blocks.note: a nappy is the British word for a diaper
a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin

explanation.surface: An epidemic traced to a kid's rubbish bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' reads as seen, but means covered in spots; the whole clue also describes the condition, with the two pieces in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: Nappy rash is red, spotty skin irritation on a baby's bottom caused by a wet or dirty diaper.

clue.text: Express disappointment with problem — it all sounds so daunting

indicators.note: sounds tells us to go by how the words are spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: aw is a cry of disappointment
a sum is an arithmetic problem, and also the whole of it all

explanation.surface: Someone groans at a task that seems overwhelming.
explanation.walkthrough: AW plus SUM, said together, is heard as AWESOME; 'it all' backs up sum as the total.
explanation.definitionFit: Awesome in its original sense means inspiring awe or dread, so overwhelming and intimidating.

clue.text: Attractive lead, perhaps taking time out for curry?

indicators.note: something taken out is removed, so a letter is dropped from the word before

blocks.note: hot means sexually attractive
lead is an example of a metal
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A tempting tip-off about a takeaway, sounding like a detective's promising clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attractive lead' looks like a promising clue, but lead is the metal; the question mark marks curry as an example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A curry is one example of a warm cooked dish served at a mealtime.

clue.text: Half of them rumble with a rhythmic sound

indicators.note: half of a word means keeping only one of its halves, here the front portion

blocks.note: the first two of four letters
the first three of six letters

explanation.surface: A group of people half-heartedly making a low, rolling noise.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of governs both words: the front half of each is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrum is a continuous rhythmic humming or strumming, like fingers drummed on a table.

clue.text: Damaged carriage lacking starter causes turbulence in flight

indicators.note: lacking its starter means the opening letter of the word is missing
something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A broken train carriage causes a commotion on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turbulence' suggests rough air, but here it is disorderly behaviour by passengers on a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Air rage is violent or aggressive passenger behaviour aboard an aircraft, a kind of disturbance mid-flight.

clue.text: Express frustration after removing clip from graphical representation

definitions.note: the answer is an exclamation used to do this

indicators.note: removing one word's letters from another takes them out of it
read as re-presentation, the letters are set out again in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Annoyance at having to cut a clip out of a chart.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C, L, I and P from GRAPHICAL to leave GRAHA, then rearrange. 'Graphical representation' looks like a chart, but the second word is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry is a spelled-out howl of exasperation, used when someone vents annoyance.

clue.text: It's shown to those getting cards

definitions.text: It's shown to those getting cards

blocks.clueFragment: It's shown to those getting cards
blocks.note: surface reading: something displayed to people receiving greetings cards or a card game hand
setter's reading: given one's cards means sacked from a job, and the sacked are shown the exit

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, being given your cards means being dismissed, from the employment documents once handed back; the idiom 'shown the door' means the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shown the door is to be ejected or dismissed, the fate of anyone fired from work.

clue.text: It measures spirits of subject as temperature drops

indicators.note: the abbreviation for temperature drops down from its place at the top of the word, lower in this down entry

blocks.note: a topic is a subject
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A device gauges people's mood as the weather turns colder.
explanation.walkthrough: The T at the top of TOPIC moves down two places in this down entry, giving OPTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An optic is a bar device fixed to an upturned bottle that dispenses a set measure of spirits.

clue.text: Finished on the double? That's a bit excessive

blocks.note: over means finished
the double asks for a second word for finished

explanation.surface: Someone completing a job at top speed is told they've gone too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the double' sounds like hurry up, but it means finished twice, with two synonyms side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdone means exaggerated or carried too far, like food overcooked or a performance overplayed.

clue.text: Complain about check on basic piece of information

indicators.note: in an across answer, a word placed on another follows it, so the check comes second

blocks.note: a bit is the basic unit of computer information
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about having to verify a fundamental fact.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer, check placed on the bit goes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bitch is a slang verb for grumbling or moaning spitefully about something.

clue.text: Dealing with old remains in a mad alcoholic rage

indicators.note: mad means crazed and out of order, so the surrounding letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk's furious outburst, comically linked to digging up the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaeology studies past human life through excavated artefacts and ruins, the old remains of earlier societies.
